setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped, Rate is /1 and every Mosaic option is at its default. The norns clock is internal at 90 BPM. A separate MIDI device is connected on port 1 and will send clock at 100 BPM when Mosaic follows it. The PARAMS menu is closed.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu and open the CLOCK group. Source reads internal: Mosaic keeps its own tempo of 90 BPM.
steps.title: Begin with internal clock

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent. Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows incoming MIDI clock, Start and Stop from the connected device and waits for them, so its own tempo no longer sets the speed.
steps.title: Select MIDI clock

steps.caption: You do nothing in this step: the connected device sends clock, a Start, more clock, then a Stop. Mosaic stays silent through the first clock pulses, begins when Start arrives, plays the phrase at the sender's 100 BPM and halts when Stop arrives. The MIDI strip below lists the notes, 0.15 seconds apart, one sixteenth at 100 BPM.
steps.title: The other device sends clock

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent back down to put Source on internal. Mosaic is on its own clock again.
steps.title: Return to internal

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the tempo row. It reads 100 BPM: while Source was midi the incoming clock set the tempo, and switching Source back does not restore your own. Turn E3 ten detents down to bring it back to 90 BPM, the tempo the project used before.
steps.title: Bring the tempo back to 90 BPM

steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play. The notes are again one sixth of a second apart, the pace of 90 BPM, as the MIDI strip shows.
steps.title: Play on the internal clock
